description: The Ultimate all-in social media automation (outreach) tool 🤖

summary.one_liner: GrowChief is an open-source, API-driven social media automation and outreach tool that runs step-by-step workflows such as connection requests and follow-up messages across social accounts.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes GrowChief as a workflow-based tool for interacting with multiple social media accounts, such as sending connection requests and follow-up messages. Workflows can be triggered through an API, and the README names n8n, Make, and Zapier as intended integration platforms. It serializes actions per account so that workflows sharing an account do not scrape at the same time, and it can run actions at a set rate. Leads added without a profile URL can be resolved through an enrichment waterfall that tries multiple providers, starting from data like email. Processing is limited to configured working hours, and the README says users can supply their own proxies. The stack is a pnpm monorepo with a React (Vite) frontend, NestJS backend and workers, Prisma on PostgreSQL by default, and Temporal as the orchestrator.
use_cases: trigger social outreach from n8n workflows
enrich leads to find social profile URLs
run outreach only during working hours
manage multiple social accounts with proxies
how_to_run: Follow the QuickStart / Installation section of the docs (the README itself only links to it)
Docker image is available; it runs headful with xvfb and opens a Chrome browser per automation
notable: Serialized per-account actions so concurrent workflows never scrape the same account simultaneously
Enrichment waterfall that tries multiple providers to find a profile URL from email or other fields
Working-hours gating so API-added leads are processed only during set hours
Uses Playwright with Patchright and simulated mouse movement for stealth
Credentials are authenticated through a method that avoids storing username and password directly
caveats: The README states that social media automation violates platform terms of service and can lead to bans, so use is at the user's own risk
Docker setup launches a full Chrome browser per run, which the README says suits only 1-2 accounts; larger scale requires a remote browser or the paid GrowChief Cloud
The README gives no concrete install commands; it links to external docs for QuickStart
